OOS_protocol.data_window: to be fixed in the registration before any data is read
OOS_protocol.train_test_boundary: prospective only for BTC (frozen plan); any other symbol needs its own registration

capacity_model.note: tiny owner scale; capacity is not the binding constraint, funding level is

economic_mechanism: Counterparty: perpetual longs pay funding to the short. Persists while net long leverage demand exists; disappears when funding falls toward zero/negative or the hurdle (financing, fees) exceeds it. The frozen BTC experiment is the registered instance; this spec is a generalisation and must not touch it.
eligibility_rules: owner already holds the spot (no spot purchase cost counted) or purchase cost is counted
perp leg only if the base asset is owned
entry: short perp when trailing funding clears the registered hurdle
exit: funding below hurdle for a registered number of settlements or margin floor
hypothesis: Holding spot against a short perpetual earns funding exceeding costs over the holding period (the delta-neutral carry this repo already runs for BTC).
prospective_protocol: only through tools/carry_prospective for BTC; other symbols require a new registration with new digests
rejection_conditions: mean funding after the registered cost model is not above the hurdle in the closed window
any parameter change after registration (invalidates the candidate, new id required)
adjusted p-value above 0.05 for any non-BTC extension
net edge after costs not positive

required_data.name: funding history for the traded symbols

required_data.gap: spot BTC OHLCV exists; basis at settlement partial (tools/basis_at_settlement)
required_data.name: spot price history and hedge-leg basis at entry/exit

required_data.gap: OKX USDT lending 1h only; not the owner's actual cost
required_data.name: borrow/financing rate for the capital held

status_note: SPECIFICATION ONLY. Nothing has been tested; this is not a winner. A bias_declaration is True only where the data needed to rule that bias out is in the repo; it is False wherever a required_data item with repo_has=false names it in declaration_keys. Such a candidate is not yet a testable specification (the verdict reports BIAS_NOT_RULED_OUT) until that data is collected.
